name: OnabotulinumtoxinA OAB dose-ranging trial
question: Which intradetrusor onabotulinumtoxinA dose balances urgency-incontinence improvement and voiding risk in idiopathic overactive bladder inadequately managed with anticholinergics?

design.population: Adults aged 18–85 years with idiopathic overactive bladder and urinary urgency incontinence for at least six months, inadequately managed with anticholinergics, with at least eight urgency-incontinence episodes weekly and eight micturitions daily at baseline; detrusor overactivity was not required.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled dose-ranging randomized trial
design.locator: Full text, Dmochowski 2010, Subjects and Figure 1, pp 2417–2418; Fowler 2012, Results and Table 1, pp 150–152

verdictNote: Week-12 pairwise P values were unreported; cumulative dose response favored doses of at least 100 U.
takeaway: In 313 patients with idiopathic overactive bladder and urgency incontinence, intradetrusor onabotulinumtoxinA 50–300 U was compared with placebo. Week-12 mean reductions varied across doses without a clear dose response; cumulative analyses favored at least 100 U, while catheterization increased with dose.

reports.label: Primary dose-ranging report
reports.citation: Dmochowski R, Chapple C, Nitti VW, et al. "Efficacy and Safety of OnabotulinumtoxinA for Idiopathic Overactive Bladder: A Double-Blind, Placebo Controlled, Randomized, Dose Ranging Trial." *J Urol.* 2010;184(6):2416-2422. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2010.08.021
reports.followUp: Week 12 primary endpoint; follow-up through week 36
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Assessments and Patient Disposition, pp 2417–2418

results.measure: 7-day bladder-diary change from baseline at week 12
results.note: Intent-to-treat ANCOVA used P ≤0.05 without multiplicity adjustment; week-12 pairwise P values and confidence intervals were not reported. A separate cumulative rank analysis showed dose response, with little added benefit above 150 U.
results.locator: Full text, Statistical Analysis and Efficacy/Patient Bladder Diary Data, pp 2417–2419

results.measure: 100% reduction in urgency-incontinence episodes at week 12; randomized arm denominators
results.note: Percentages are reported in the primary text; counts use randomized-arm denominators and are implied by the rounded percentages.
results.locator: Full text, Efficacy/Patient Bladder Diary Data, p 2419; Figure 1, p 2418

harms.label: Urinary tract infection
harms.locator: Full text, Table 1 and Safety, pp 2419–2420
harms.note: Safety population; UTI was not required to be culture confirmed; UTI was one of two adverse events reported as more frequent with active treatment than placebo at P <0.05.

harms.label: Urinary retention
harms.locator: Full text, Table 1 and Safety, pp 2419–2420
harms.note: Safety population; PVR ≥200 mL was added as an adverse-event definition of retention during the study; all affected patients could void spontaneously.

harms.label: Postvoid residual and PVR-related catheterization
harms.locator: Full text, Tables 1–2 and Safety, pp 2419–2420
harms.note: Safety population; catheterization was PVR related, either intermittent or indwelling. Among patients with posttreatment PVR ≥200 mL, 33/55 (60.0%) were catheterized.

harms.label: Serious adverse events
harms.value: 34/311 treated patients (10.9%) reported 45 serious adverse events; two were study-drug related: urinary retention at 100 U and gastroparesis flare at 50 U.
harms.locator: Full text, Safety, p 2419; Table 1, p 2420

delivery.label: Treatment administration
delivery.value: Single cystoscopic treatment of 50, 100, 150, 200, or 300 U onabotulinumtoxinA or placebo in 20 detrusor injections of 0.5 mL each, evenly distributed while avoiding the trigone and dome; intravesical 1%–2% lidocaine or equivalent, with optional sedation.

delivery.label: Study completion
delivery.value: 272/313 (86.9%) completed 36 weeks; 41/313 (13.1%) discontinued; none discontinued because of treatment-related adverse events.
delivery.locator: Full text, Patient Disposition, p 2418; Discussion, p 2420

reports.label: Urodynamic analysis
reports.citation: Rovner E, Kennelly M, Schulte-Baukloh H, et al. "Urodynamic Results and Clinical Outcomes with Intradetrusor Injections of OnabotulinumtoxinA in a Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Dose-Finding Study in Idiopathic Overactive Bladder." *Neurourol Urodyn.* 2011;30(4):556-562. doi:10.1002/nau.21021

results.endpoint: Maximum cystometric capacity and volume at first involuntary detrusor contraction
results.note: Improvements generally decreased by week 36; no difference in clinical outcomes by baseline detrusor overactivity status was reported.

results.endpoint: No urgency urinary incontinence on diary
results.note: Active-dose range endpoints only are stated in the abstract; arm denominators come from ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00168454 Participant Flow.
results.locator: PubMed abstract, Results; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00168454, Participant Flow, Started

harms.label: Postvoid residual above 200 mL
harms.note: More common with doses above 150 U; arm rates not provided.

reports.label: Quality-of-life analysis
reports.citation: Fowler CJ, Auerbach S, Ginsberg D, et al. "OnabotulinumtoxinA Improves Health-Related Quality of Life in Patients with Urinary Incontinence Due to Idiopathic Overactive Bladder: A 36-Week, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Randomized, Dose-Ranging Trial." *Eur Urol.* 2012;62(1):148-157. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2012.03.005
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Patients and Methods, pp 149–150

results.measure: Mean I-QOL total-score change from baseline at week 12; intent-to-treat analysis
results.note: Exploratory endpoint; total-score improvements versus placebo were significant for all doses ≥100 U from weeks 2 through 36; subscale improvements were significant through week 24. P values were unadjusted for multiplicity; confidence intervals were not reported.
results.locator: Full text, Assessments and Statistical analysis, pp 149–150; Results and Figures 3–4, pp 150–153

results.measure: Mean change from baseline at week 12; intent-to-treat analysis

values.d50: No significant difference vs placebo; 57 randomized
values.d100: Significantly greater reduction than placebo; 54 randomized
values.d150: Significantly greater reduction than placebo; 49 randomized
values.d200: Significantly greater reduction than placebo; 53 randomized
values.d300: Significantly greater reduction than placebo; 56 randomized

results.note: The paper reports between-group mean-improvement differences ranging from −2.7 to −10.8 points, but not arm-specific numeric estimates in text; all doses ≥100 U differed from placebo at week 12.
results.locator: Full text, Results, King's Health Questionnaire symptom component and Figure 5, pp 152–154

results.measure: Mean change from baseline at week 36; intent-to-treat analysis
results.note: At 300 U, physical functioning, role-physical, bodily pain and vitality differed from placebo; at 200 U, role-physical differed. Pairwise P values are in Table 2; no confidence intervals reported.
results.locator: Full text, Table 2 and Results, SF-36, pp 152–154
